scenario.title: Specification Document Review
scenario.initial_description: An engineer reviews a specification document to check whether new features are reflected correctly and whether there are typos or missing details.

reference_workflow.goal: Review a specification document for feature coverage, consistency, and editorial errors.

activities.name: Collect document and related change list
Compare feature changes with document content

automation_opportunities.rationale: Feature coverage can be checked by comparing change lists and document sections.
Terminology, formatting, and typo checks can be automated.
Review comments can be grouped by section, severity, and owner.

activities.name: Check for Typos and Language Errors
outputs: List of Typos and Language Issues

activities.name: Compile Review Findings
inputs: List of Typos and Language Issues

decisions.condition: Are all new features correctly reflected in the specification?

branches.note: Flag missing or incorrect feature descriptions

decisions.condition: Are there typos, language errors, or missing details found?
Is the updated specification document satisfactory?

exceptions.description: Specification document is not accessible or is missing
exceptions.handling: Engineer escalates to document owner to provide the correct document version before review proceeds

exceptions.description: Feature requirements list is outdated or unavailable
exceptions.handling: Engineer requests updated requirements from the relevant stakeholder before proceeding with feature coverage review

exceptions.description: Document owner is unresponsive after review report submission
exceptions.handling: Engineer escalates to team lead to follow up and ensure timely document update

automation_opportunities.target: A3 - Check for Typos and Language Errors
automation_opportunities.rationale: Natural language processing tools can automatically scan specification documents for spelling errors, grammatical issues, and stylistic inconsistencies, significantly reducing manual effort and improving consistency.
constraints: Tool must support technical and domain-specific vocabulary
False positive rate must be manageable for engineers

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated diff and traceability tools can compare the specification document against a structured feature requirements list to flag features not mentioned or incompletely described, partially automating coverage checks.
constraints: Feature requirements must be in a structured, machine-readable format
Semantic matching may require human validation for ambiguous cases

automation_opportunities.rationale: Template-based validation tools can check whether all mandatory sections and fields in the specification are populated, automating detection of structurally missing information.
constraints: Effectiveness limited to structurally defined missing details; semantic gaps still require human judgment

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated aggregation tools can consolidate findings from spell-check, coverage analysis, and template validation into a structured review report, reducing manual compilation effort.
constraints: Engineer must validate and approve auto-generated report before submission

automation_opportunities.rationale: Workflow automation can handle routing and notification of the review report to the document owner upon engineer approval, eliminating manual submission steps.
constraints: Engineer must explicitly approve submission to maintain accountability

automation_opportunities.target: D1 - Are all new features correctly reflected in the specification?
automation_opportunities.rationale: If feature requirements are structured and machine-readable, automated traceability analysis can partially resolve this decision, flagging gaps for engineer confirmation.
constraints: Ambiguous or loosely defined requirements reduce reliability of automated decision
Human override must always be available

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated document retrieval triggered by a review task assignment can eliminate the manual step of locating and opening the correct document version.
constraints: Document Management System must support API-based retrieval
Access permissions must be correctly configured

assumptions: A structured Feature Requirements List exists and is available to the engineer prior to the review.
The specification document is stored in a Document Management System with version control.
The engineer is responsible for both language quality checks and feature coverage checks.
A document owner exists who is responsible for updating the specification based on review findings.
The review cycle may iterate if the updated document does not meet the engineer's expectations.
Review findings are compiled into a formal report rather than communicated informally.
Notifications to the document owner are handled through the Document Management System.
The review is conducted on a single document version at a time.
